methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $575M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
VulcanForms, founded by John Hart and Martin Feldmann, is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $575M+ to date. The comparable universe includes one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, a formal peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds—only 10 same-sector peers exist, but none yielded three or more datapoints within narrow valuation tiers.

Given this constraint, the valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($575M) as a proxy for enterprise value, a typical late-stage step-up multiplier of 1.2x is applied, yielding an implied valuation of $690M. This single-method triangulation produces a median estimate of $690M, with a low range of $586M (representing a 1.02x step-up) and a high range of $793M (1.38x). The stage-progression method is the only quantitatively supportable approach given data constraints.

The $690M median valuation carries material uncertainty. Peer-based triangulation cannot be reliably executed without sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables. Key variables affecting actual valuation include customer concentration, gross margins, and growth trajectory relative to the broader robotics sector.
